title: What does Clawback do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of Clawback and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, Clawback allows an eligible issuer to take back its own issued tokens from a holder. [1]

Trust-line token clawback depends on the issuer enabling its clawback permission under the account-setting prerequisites. It is not an XRP reversal or a general right to seize other issuers' assets. MPTs have their own issuance capabilities. Check the exact holder, issuance and allowed amount before treating a compliance policy as enforceable ledger authority. [1]

The Clawback reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using Clawback, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
